units.zh: 孔子曰：「六藝於治一也。
units.en: Confucius said: "The Six Arts all serve a single purpose in governance.
units.literal: Confucius said: "The Six Arts are united in governance.

units.zh: 禮以節人，樂以發和，書以道事，詩以達意，易以神化，春秋以義。」
units.en: The Rites temper human conduct, Music inspires harmony, the Documents illuminate affairs of state, the Odes give voice to the heart's intent, the Changes reveal the workings of the divine, and the Spring and Autumn Annals uphold righteousness."
units.literal: Ritual regulates people, Music brings forth harmony, the Documents speak of affairs, the Odes convey meaning, the Changes work spiritual transformation, and the Spring and Autumn Annals uphold righteousness."

units.zh: 太史公曰：天道恢恢，豈不大哉！
units.en: The Grand Historian remarks: How vast and all-embracing is the Way of Heaven!
units.literal: The Grand Historian says: The Way of Heaven is vast and all-encompassing — is it not great!

units.zh: 談言微中，亦可以解紛。
units.en: A well-placed jest, hitting subtly upon the truth, can untangle even the most knotted affairs.
units.literal: Casual words that subtly hit the mark can also resolve disputes.

units.zh: 淳于髡者，齊之贅婿也。
units.en: Chunyu Kun was a man of Qi who had married into his wife's family as a live-in son-in-law.
units.literal: Chunyu Kun was a live-in son-in-law from the state of Qi.

units.zh: 長不滿七尺，滑稽多辯，數使諸侯，未嘗屈辱。
units.en: He stood less than seven chi tall, yet he was quick-witted and sharp-tongued. Sent on missions to the feudal lords time and again, he never once suffered disgrace.
units.literal: He stood less than seven chi tall, was witty and eloquent, and served as envoy to the feudal lords many times without ever being humiliated.

units.zh: 齊威王之時喜隱，好為淫樂長夜之飲，沈湎不治，委政卿大夫。
units.en: King Wei of Qi delighted in riddles. He gave himself over to pleasure and caroused through the night, sinking into dissipation and neglecting the affairs of state, which he left entirely to his ministers.
units.literal: During the time of King Wei of Qi, the king was fond of riddles, indulged in excessive pleasures and all-night drinking, wallowed in dissipation and neglected governance, delegating affairs of state to his ministers and grandees.

units.zh: 百官荒亂，諸侯并侵，國且危亡，在於旦暮，左右莫敢諫。
units.en: The court officials descended into chaos, rival lords invaded from every quarter, and the state teetered on the brink of ruin — its fall a matter of days. Yet not one of the king's attendants dared speak a word of remonstrance.
units.literal: The hundred officials fell into disorder, the feudal lords encroached from all sides, the state was on the verge of collapse — its destruction could come any morning or evening — yet none around the king dared to remonstrate.

units.zh: 淳于髡說之以隱曰：「國中有大鳥，止王之庭，三年不蜚又不鳴，不知此鳥何也？」
units.en: Chunyu Kun approached the king with a riddle: "In our kingdom there is a great bird that has roosted in Your Majesty's courtyard for three full years. It neither flies nor sings. What manner of bird might this be?"
units.literal: Chunyu Kun persuaded the king with a riddle, saying: "There is a great bird in the kingdom that has perched in the king's court for three years without flying or crying out — do you know what bird this is?"

units.zh: 王曰：「此鳥不飛則已，一飛沖天；
units.en: The king replied: "This bird — if it does not fly, so be it. But once it takes flight, it will soar straight to the heavens.
units.literal: The king said: "This bird — if it does not fly, then so be it, but once it flies it will soar to the heavens;

units.zh: 不鳴則已，一鳴驚人。」
units.en: If it does not cry out, so be it. But once it cries out, it will astonish the world."
units.literal: If it does not cry then so be it, but once it cries it will astound everyone."

units.zh: 於是乃朝諸縣令長七十二人，賞一人，誅一人，奮兵而出。
units.en: With that, the king summoned his seventy-two county magistrates to court. He rewarded one and put another to death, then roused his armies and marched forth.
units.literal: Thereupon he summoned the seventy-two county magistrates to court, rewarded one, executed one, and mobilized his armies to march forth.

units.zh: 諸侯振驚，皆還齊侵地。
units.en: The feudal lords were shaken with alarm. Every one of them returned the lands they had seized from Qi.
units.literal: The feudal lords were shaken and alarmed, and all returned the territories they had seized from Qi.

units.zh: 威行三十六年。
units.en: His authority held sway for thirty-six years.
units.literal: His prestige lasted for thirty-six years.

units.zh: 語在田完世家中。
units.en: The full account can be found in the Hereditary House of Lord Tian Wan.
units.literal: This account is in the Hereditary House of Tian Wan.

units.zh: 威王八年，楚大發兵加齊。
units.en: In the eighth year of King Wei's reign, Chu mobilized a massive army and attacked Qi.
units.literal: In the eighth year of King Wei, Chu launched a great army against Qi.

units.zh: 齊王使淳于髡之趙請救兵，齎金百斤，車馬十駟。
units.en: The King of Qi dispatched Chunyu Kun to Zhao to beg for reinforcements, equipping him with a hundred catties of gold and ten teams of horses with chariots.
units.literal: The King of Qi sent Chunyu Kun to Zhao to request rescue troops, bearing a hundred catties of gold and ten four-horse chariots.

units.zh: 淳于髡仰天大笑，冠纓索絕。
units.en: Chunyu Kun threw back his head and roared with laughter — so hard that the chin-straps of his cap snapped clean through.
units.literal: Chunyu Kun threw back his head toward the sky and laughed greatly, until the strings of his cap snapped.

units.zh: 王曰：「先生少之乎？」
units.en: The king asked: "Does the master find the gifts insufficient?"
units.literal: The king said: "Does the master consider it too little?"

units.zh: 髡曰：「何敢！」
units.en: Kun replied: "I would never dare!"
units.literal: Kun said: "How would I dare!"

units.zh: 王曰：「笑豈有說乎？」
units.en: The king pressed: "Then what was the meaning of that laugh?"
units.literal: The king said: "Does the laugh have an explanation?"

units.zh: 髡曰：「今者臣從東方來，見道傍有禳田者，操一豚蹄，酒一盂，祝曰：『甌窶滿篝，汙邪滿車，五穀蕃熟，穰穰滿家。』
units.en: Kun said: "Just now, as your servant was traveling from the east, I saw a man by the roadside performing a prayer over his fields. He held up a single pig's trotter and a bowl of wine and prayed: 'Let the hilltop baskets overflow! Let the lowland carts be piled high! Let the five grains ripen in plenty, and harvests fill my house!'
units.literal: Kun said: "Just now your servant was coming from the east, and saw by the roadside a man performing a ritual to protect his fields, holding a single pig's trotter and a bowl of wine, praying: 'May the high-ground baskets overflow, may the lowland carts be heaped full, may the five grains ripen in abundance, may bountiful harvests fill my house.'

units.zh: 臣見其所持者狹而所欲者奢，故笑之。」
units.en: I saw that his offering was paltry, but his prayers were grand — and so I could not help but laugh."
units.literal: Your servant saw that what he offered was meager while what he desired was extravagant, and so I laughed at him."

units.zh: 於是齊威王乃益齎黃金千溢，白璧十雙，車馬百駟。
units.en: At this, King Wei increased the gifts to a thousand yi of gold, ten pairs of white jade discs, and a hundred teams of horses with chariots.
units.literal: Thereupon King Wei of Qi increased the gifts to a thousand yi of gold, ten pairs of white jade discs, and a hundred four-horse chariots.

units.zh: 髡辭而行，至趙。
units.en: Kun took his leave and set out for Zhao.
units.literal: Kun took his leave and traveled, arriving in Zhao.

units.zh: 趙王與之精兵十萬，革車千乘。
units.en: The King of Zhao provided a hundred thousand crack troops and a thousand war chariots.
units.literal: The King of Zhao gave him one hundred thousand elite soldiers and a thousand leather-covered war chariots.

units.zh: 楚聞之，夜引兵而去。
units.en: When Chu received word, they pulled back their forces under cover of night.
units.literal: When Chu heard of this, they withdrew their army at night and left.

units.zh: 威王大說，置酒後宮，召髡賜之酒。
units.en: King Wei was overjoyed. He laid out a feast in the inner palace and summoned Kun to share in the wine.
units.literal: King Wei was greatly pleased, held a banquet in the rear palace, summoned Kun and bestowed wine upon him.

units.zh: 問曰：「先生能飲幾何而醉？」
units.en: He asked: "How much can the master drink before he gets drunk?"
units.literal: He asked: "How much can the master drink before becoming drunk?"

units.zh: 對曰：「臣飲一斗亦醉，一石亦醉。」
units.en: Kun answered: "Your servant gets drunk after a single peck, and also gets drunk after a full bushel."
units.literal: He replied: "Your servant becomes drunk on one dou, and also becomes drunk on one dan."

units.zh: 威王曰：「先生飲一斗而醉，惡能飲一石哉！
units.en: King Wei said: "If the master gets drunk after a single peck, how could he possibly drink a whole bushel?
units.literal: King Wei said: "If the master gets drunk on one dou, how could he drink a whole dan!

units.zh: 其說可得聞乎？」
units.en: Pray explain this to me."
units.literal: May I hear the explanation?"

units.zh: 髡曰：「賜酒大王之前，執法在傍，御史在後，髡恐懼俯伏而飲，不過一斗徑醉矣。
units.en: Kun said: "When I am granted the honor of drinking before Your Majesty, with the marshal of law at my side and the imperial censor at my back, I drink in fear and trembling, bowing low to the ground — a single peck is enough to make me drunk.
units.literal: Kun said: "When bestowed wine before the Great King, with the law enforcer beside me and the censor behind me, Kun drinks in fear and trembling, prostrate and bowed — after no more than a dou I am quite drunk.

units.zh: 若親有嚴客，髡帣韝鞠跽，待酒於前，時賜餘瀝，奉觴上壽，數起，飲不過二斗徑醉矣。
units.en: When my parents entertain honored guests, I tuck up my sleeves and kneel attentively, pouring wine and waiting upon them. Now and then they bestow the leftover drops, and I raise my cup to toast their health, rising and sitting again and again — after two pecks, I am drunk.
units.literal: If my parents have honored guests, Kun tucks up his sleeves and kneels upright, waiting upon them with wine, occasionally receiving the dregs they bestow, and I raise my cup to toast their health, rising again and again — after no more than two dou I am quite drunk.

units.zh: 若朋友交遊，久不相見，卒然相睹，歡然道故，私情相語，飲可五六斗徑醉矣。
units.en: When old friends who have long been parted meet again by chance, joyfully recounting the past and sharing their inmost thoughts — then I can drink five or six pecks before I am drunk.
units.literal: If friends and companions who have not seen each other for a long time suddenly meet, joyfully recount old times, and share intimate feelings in conversation, I can drink five or six dou before becoming drunk.

units.zh: 若乃州閭之會，男女雜坐，行酒稽留，六博投壺，相引為曹，握手無罰，目眙不禁，前有墮珥，后有遺簪，髡竊樂此，飲可八斗而醉二參。
units.en: At a neighborhood gathering where men and women mingle freely, the wine cups circulate without end, and there are games of dice and pitch-pot. People pull one another into little groups, hands clasp without forfeit, bold glances go unchecked, earrings fall unnoticed to the floor, and hairpins slip loose behind. This is where I secretly revel, and I can drink eight pecks before I am two-thirds gone.
units.literal: If there is a neighborhood gathering where men and women sit mixed together, wine circulates without pause, there are games of liubo and pitch-pot, people pull each other into groups, clasping hands without penalty, staring without prohibition, earrings dropped in front and hairpins lost behind — I secretly delight in this, and can drink eight dou, being two-thirds drunk.

units.zh: 日暮酒闌，合尊促坐，男女同席，履舄交錯，杯盤狼藉，堂上燭滅，主人留髡而送客，羅襦襟解，微聞薌澤，當此之時，髡心最歡，能飲一石。
units.en: As dusk falls and the feast winds down, the wine vessels are pushed together and the seats drawn close. Men and women share the same mat, their footwear tangled on the floor and cups and dishes scattered in disarray. The candles in the hall gutter out. The host keeps Kun behind while seeing the other guests to the door. Silk jackets fall open at the collar, and the faintest trace of perfume drifts through the air. At such a moment, my heart brims with delight — and I can drink a full bushel.
units.literal: As evening falls and the wine wanes, cups are combined and seats pressed close, men and women share the same mat, shoes and sandals lie tangled, cups and plates strewn about in disarray, the candles in the hall are extinguished, the host keeps Kun while seeing other guests off, silk jackets fall open at the breast, and a faint fragrance drifts through the air — at such a moment, my heart is most joyful, and I can drink a full dan.

units.zh: 故曰酒極則亂，樂極則悲；
units.en: The saying goes: when wine goes to excess, chaos follows; when pleasure reaches its height, sorrow awaits.
units.literal: Therefore, it is said: when wine reaches its extreme there is disorder, when pleasure reaches its extreme there is sorrow;

units.zh: 萬事盡然，言不可極，極之而衰。」
units.en: All things under heaven follow this same law — nothing should be pushed to the extreme, for at the extreme comes only decline."
units.literal: All things are the same in this — they say one must not go to extremes, for at the extreme comes decline."

units.zh: 以諷諫焉。
units.en: With this, he delivered his remonstrance through allegory.
units.literal: By this he offered indirect admonishment.

units.zh: 齊王曰：「善。」
units.en: The King of Qi said: "Well spoken."
units.literal: The King of Qi said: "Excellent."

units.zh: 乃罷長夜之飲，以髡為諸侯主客。
units.en: He put an end to the all-night carousing and appointed Kun as the master of ceremonies for receiving envoys from the feudal lords.
units.literal: He then ceased the all-night drinking and appointed Kun as the master of ceremonies for receiving the feudal lords.

units.zh: 宗室置酒，髡嘗在側。
units.en: Whenever the royal house held a feast, Kun was always at the king's side.
units.literal: Whenever the royal clan held banquets, Kun was always at his side.

units.zh: 其後百餘年，楚有優孟。
units.en: More than a hundred years after this, there arose in Chu a jester called You Meng.
units.literal: More than a hundred years later, Chu had You Meng.

units.zh: 優孟，故楚之樂人也。
units.en: You Meng had been an entertainer in the service of Chu.
units.literal: You Meng was originally a musician of Chu.

units.zh: 長八尺，多辯，常以談笑諷諫。
units.en: He stood eight chi tall, was quick with words, and always delivered his counsel through wit and laughter.
units.literal: He was eight chi tall, highly eloquent, and always used humor and jest to offer indirect admonishment.

units.zh: 楚莊王之時，有所愛馬，衣以文繡，置之華屋之下，席以露床，啗以棗脯。
units.en: King Zhuang of Chu had a horse he doted on. He dressed it in embroidered silks, housed it beneath a splendid canopy, bedded it upon an open couch, and fed it dates and dried meat.
units.literal: During the time of King Zhuang of Chu, the king had a beloved horse which he dressed in embroidered silks, housed beneath a magnificent canopy, bedded on an open couch, and fed with dates and dried meat.

units.zh: 馬病肥死，使群臣喪之，欲以棺槨大夫禮葬之。
units.en: The horse grew fat, fell ill, and died. The king commanded his officials to observe mourning for it, and he wished to bury it in a double coffin with the full rites accorded a grandee.
units.literal: The horse fell ill from overfeeding and died. The king ordered his ministers to mourn it and wished to bury it in an inner and outer coffin with the rites due a grandee.

units.zh: 左右爭之，以為不可。
units.en: The king's attendants objected, insisting that such a thing was improper.
units.literal: Those around him argued against it, considering it improper.

units.zh: 王下令曰：「有敢以馬諫者，罪至死。」
units.en: The king issued a decree: "Anyone who dares remonstrate with me over the horse shall be put to death."
units.literal: The king issued a decree: "Anyone who dares to remonstrate about the horse shall be punished with death."

units.zh: 優孟聞之，入殿門。
units.en: When You Meng heard of this, he strode into the great hall.
units.literal: When You Meng heard this, he entered through the palace gates.

units.zh: 仰天大哭。
units.en: He threw back his head and wept aloud to the heavens.
units.literal: He looked up to the sky and wailed loudly.

units.zh: 王驚而問其故。
units.en: Startled, the king demanded to know the cause of his grief.
units.literal: The king was startled and asked him the reason.

units.zh: 優孟曰：「馬者王之所愛也，以楚國堂堂之大，何求不得，而以大夫禮葬之，薄，請以人君禮葬之。」
units.en: You Meng said: "The horse was Your Majesty's beloved. With all the grandeur and might of Chu at your command, what could be beyond your reach? But to bury it with the rites of a mere grandee — that is too paltry by far! I beg that you bury it with the full rites due a sovereign lord."
units.literal: You Meng said: "The horse was the king's beloved. With the great and mighty state of Chu, what could be unobtainable? Yet to bury it with the rites of a grandee — that is too meager. I beg that it be buried with the rites due a sovereign."

units.zh: 王曰：「何如？」
units.en: The king asked: "And how would that be done?"
units.literal: The king said: "How so?"

units.zh: 對曰：「臣請以彫玉為棺，文梓為槨，楩楓豫章為題湊，發甲卒為穿壙，老弱負土，齊趙陪位於前，韓魏翼衛其后，廟食太牢，奉以萬戶之邑。
units.en: He replied: "Let the inner coffin be carved of jade, the outer coffin fashioned from figured catalpa, and the frame built of nanmu, maple, and camphor. Conscript armored troops to dig the grave and the old and frail to carry the earth. Let Qi and Zhao stand in attendance before the tomb, with Han and Wei flanking it in guard. Erect a temple where the Great Sacrifice of ox, sheep, and pig is offered, and grant the horse a fief of ten thousand households.
units.literal: He replied: "I request that carved jade be used for the inner coffin, patterned catalpa for the outer coffin, and the finest timber of nanmu, maple, and camphor for the frame. Armored soldiers should be conscripted to dig the tomb, the old and frail to carry the earth. Qi and Zhao shall stand in attendance before it, Han and Wei shall guard its flanks. A temple shall be erected where it is fed the Great Sacrifice, and it shall be granted a fief of ten thousand households.

units.zh: 諸侯聞之，皆知大王賤人而貴馬也。」
units.en: When the feudal lords hear of this, they will all understand that Your Majesty prizes horses above human beings."
units.literal: When the feudal lords hear of this, they will all know that the Great King values horses above men."

units.zh: 王曰：「寡人之過一至此乎！
units.en: The king exclaimed: "Can my folly truly have gone so far!
units.literal: The king said: "Has my fault really gone this far!

units.zh: 為之柰何？」
units.en: What then should be done?"
units.literal: What shall be done about it?"

units.zh: 優孟曰：「請為大王六畜葬之。
units.en: You Meng said: "I suggest Your Majesty bury it as one buries any beast of the barnyard.
units.literal: You Meng said: "I suggest burying it for the Great King as one would the six domestic animals.

units.zh: 以壟灶為槨，銅歷為棺，齎以薑棗，薦以木蘭，祭以糧稻，衣以火光，葬之於人腹腸。」
units.en: Let an earthen stove serve as the outer coffin and a bronze cauldron as the inner one. Season it with ginger and dates, garnish it with magnolia bark, make offerings of grain and rice, dress it in robes of flame — and bury it in the bellies of men."
units.literal: Use an earthen oven as the outer coffin and a bronze cauldron as the inner coffin, season it with ginger and dates, garnish it with magnolia bark, sacrifice to it with rice and grain, dress it with fire, and bury it in the bellies of men."

units.zh: 於是王乃使以馬屬太官，無令天下久聞也。
units.en: At this, the king had the horse sent to the imperial kitchen, eager that the world should hear no more of the affair.
units.literal: Thereupon the king ordered the horse to be handed over to the Grand Provisioner, so that the world would not hear of the matter any longer.

units.zh: 楚相孫叔敖知其賢人也，善待之。
units.en: Sun Shuao, the Chancellor of Chu, recognized You Meng as a man of true worth and treated him with great courtesy.
units.literal: The Chancellor of Chu, Sun Shuao, recognized You Meng as a worthy man and treated him well.

units.zh: 病且死，屬其子曰：「我死，汝必貧困。
units.en: When Sun Shuao lay on his deathbed, he charged his son: "After I am gone, you will surely fall into poverty.
units.literal: When Sun Shuao fell ill and was about to die, he charged his son, saying: "When I die, you will surely fall into poverty.

units.zh: 若往見優孟，言我孫叔敖之子也。」
units.en: When that time comes, go to You Meng and tell him that you are the son of Sun Shuao."
units.literal: Go and see You Meng, and tell him you are the son of Sun Shuao."

units.zh: 居數年，其子窮困負薪，逢優孟，與言曰：「我，孫叔敖子也。
units.en: Some years later, the son had indeed fallen into destitution and was carrying firewood for a living. He chanced upon You Meng and said: "I am the son of Sun Shuao.
units.literal: After several years, Sun Shuao's son was reduced to poverty and carrying firewood on his back. He encountered You Meng and spoke to him, saying: "I am the son of Sun Shuao.

units.zh: 父且死時，屬我貧困往見優孟。」
units.en: On his deathbed, my father told me that when I fell into poverty, I should seek out You Meng."
units.literal: When my father was about to die, he instructed me that in poverty I should go see You Meng."

units.zh: 優孟曰：「若無遠有所之。」
units.en: You Meng said: "Stay close by. Do not go wandering off."
units.literal: You Meng said: "Do not go far away."

units.zh: 即為孫叔敖衣冠，抵掌談語。
units.en: He then donned the robes and cap that Sun Shuao had once worn, clapping his hands as he practiced speech and bearing.
units.literal: He then put on the robes and cap of Sun Shuao, and clapped his hands while conversing.

units.zh: 歲餘，像孫叔敖，楚王及左右不能別也。
units.en: After more than a year of practice, his impersonation of Sun Shuao was so perfect that neither the King of Chu nor his attendants could tell the two apart.
units.literal: After more than a year, he so resembled Sun Shuao that the King of Chu and those around him could not tell the difference.

units.zh: 莊王置酒，優孟前為壽。
units.en: At a banquet held by King Zhuang, You Meng came forward to offer a toast to the king's health.
units.literal: King Zhuang held a banquet, and You Meng came forward to offer a toast.

units.zh: 莊王大驚，以為孫叔敖復生也，欲以為相。
units.en: King Zhuang was astonished, convinced that Sun Shuao had returned from the dead. He wanted to appoint him chancellor on the spot.
units.literal: King Zhuang was greatly startled, believing Sun Shuao had come back to life, and wished to make him chancellor.

units.zh: 優孟曰：「請歸與婦計之，三日而為相。」
units.en: You Meng said: "Allow me to go home and consult with my wife. In three days I shall accept the chancellorship."
units.literal: You Meng said: "Allow me to go home and discuss it with my wife, and in three days I will serve as chancellor."

units.zh: 莊王許之。
units.en: King Zhuang agreed.
units.literal: King Zhuang granted his request.

units.zh: 三日後，優孟復來。
units.en: Three days later, You Meng came back.
units.literal: Three days later, You Meng returned.

units.zh: 王曰：「婦言謂何？」
units.en: The king asked: "And what did your wife have to say?"
units.literal: The king asked: "What did your wife say?"

units.zh: 孟曰：「婦言慎無為，楚相不足為也。
units.en: Meng said: "My wife urged me in the strongest terms to decline. She said the chancellorship of Chu is not worth having.
units.literal: Meng said: "My wife warned me to be careful and not to accept, saying the chancellorship of Chu is not worth holding.

units.zh: 如孫叔敖之為楚相，盡忠為廉以治楚，楚王得以霸。
units.en: Consider Sun Shuao as chancellor — he poured out his loyalty and served with perfect integrity, governing Chu so well that the king rose to become hegemon.
units.literal: Take Sun Shuao as Chancellor of Chu — he devoted himself utterly to loyalty and integrity in governing Chu, and the King of Chu thereby achieved hegemony.

units.zh: 今死，其子無立錐之地，貧困負薪以自飲食。
units.en: Now that he is dead, his son has not a pin's breadth of land to stand on. He carries firewood on his back just to keep from starving.
units.literal: Now that he is dead, his son has not a pin's breadth of land to stand on, reduced to poverty and carrying firewood to feed himself.

units.zh: 必如孫叔敖，不如自殺。」
units.en: If being chancellor means ending up like Sun Shuao, one might as well take one's own life."
units.literal: If one must end up like Sun Shuao, it would be better to kill oneself."

units.zh: 因歌曰：「山居耕田苦，難以得食。
units.en: Then he sang: "To dwell in the hills and plow the fields is bitter toil — hard even to keep body and soul together.
units.literal: He then sang: "Living in the mountains and plowing the fields is bitter toil, and it is hard to get food.

units.zh: 起而為吏，身貪鄙者餘財，不顧恥辱。
units.en: Rise to become an official, and the greedy and base among them grow rich, caring nothing for shame or disgrace.
units.literal: If one rises up to become an official, those who are greedy and base gain surplus wealth and heed no shame or disgrace.

units.zh: 身死家室富，又恐受賕枉法，為姦觸大罪，身死而家滅。
units.en: They die with their families wealthy — yet there is always the fear of taking bribes and perverting justice, of committing a crime so grave that one dies and one's whole household is destroyed.
units.literal: They die with their households wealthy, yet one must also fear accepting bribes and bending the law, committing villainy and incurring great crimes, dying with one's entire family destroyed.

units.zh: 貪吏安可為也！
units.en: How can anyone bear to be a corrupt official!
units.literal: How can one be a corrupt official!

units.zh: 念為廉吏，奉法守職，竟死不敢為非。
units.en: Think instead of being an honest official — upholding the law, fulfilling one's duties, never once daring to do wrong until the very day of one's death.
units.literal: Consider being an honest official, upholding the law and fulfilling one's duties, dying at last without ever daring to do wrong.

units.zh: 廉吏安可為也！
units.en: But how can anyone bear to be an honest official either!
units.literal: How can one be an honest official!

units.zh: 楚相孫叔敖持廉至死，方今妻子窮困負薪而食，不足為也！」
units.en: Sun Shuao, Chancellor of Chu, held fast to his integrity unto death — yet today his wife and children carry firewood on their backs just to eat. It is not worth doing!"
units.literal: The Chancellor of Chu, Sun Shuao, maintained his integrity until death, yet now his wife and children are reduced to poverty, carrying firewood for food — it is not worth doing!"

units.zh: 於是莊王謝優孟，乃召孫叔敖子，封之寢丘四百戶，以奉其祀。
units.en: At this, King Zhuang thanked You Meng. He summoned the son of Sun Shuao and enfeoffed him with four hundred households at Qinqiu, so that the ancestral sacrifices might be maintained.
units.literal: Thereupon King Zhuang thanked You Meng, summoned the son of Sun Shuao, and enfeoffed him with four hundred households at Qinqiu to maintain the family sacrifices.

units.zh: 后十世不絕。
units.en: The family line continued unbroken for ten generations.
units.literal: For ten generations afterward, the line was not cut off.

units.zh: 此知可以言時矣。
units.en: This was a man who understood the art of speaking at the right moment.
units.literal: This shows the wisdom of knowing when to speak.

units.zh: 其後二百餘年，秦有優旃。
units.en: More than two hundred years after this, there arose in Qin a jester called You Zhan.
units.literal: More than two hundred years later, Qin had You Zhan.

units.zh: 優旃者，秦倡侏儒也。
units.en: You Zhan was a dwarf entertainer in the court of Qin.
units.literal: You Zhan was an entertainer and dwarf of Qin.

units.zh: 善為笑言，然合於大道，秦始皇時，置酒而天雨，陛楯者皆沾寒。
units.en: He was a master of witty remarks, yet his jests always struck at the greater truth. During the reign of the First Emperor, a banquet was being held when rain began to fall, and the guards standing watch on the palace steps were soaked through and shivering.
units.literal: He was skilled at making jests, yet they always accorded with the great Way. During the time of the First Emperor of Qin, a banquet was held while it rained from the sky, and the palace guards standing on the steps were all drenched and cold.

units.zh: 優旃見而哀之，謂之曰：「汝欲休乎？」
units.en: You Zhan saw their misery and felt pity for them. He called out: "Would you like a rest?"
units.literal: You Zhan saw them and pitied them, and said to them: "Do you want to rest?"

units.zh: 陛楯者皆曰：「幸甚。」
units.en: The guards all cried: "We would be most grateful!"
units.literal: The guards all said: "That would be most fortunate."

units.zh: 優旃曰：「我即呼汝，汝疾應曰諾。」
units.en: You Zhan said: "When I call out to you, answer 'Aye!' as quick as you can."
units.literal: You Zhan said: "When I call out to you, answer 'Yes!' at once."

units.zh: 居有頃，殿上上壽呼萬歲。
units.en: Before long, a toast was raised in the great hall and the cry of "Ten thousand years!" rang out.
units.literal: After a short time, a toast was raised in the hall and the cry of "Ten thousand years!" went up.

units.zh: 優旃臨檻大呼曰：「陛楯郎！」
units.en: You Zhan leaned over the balustrade and bellowed: "Gentlemen of the guard!"
units.literal: You Zhan leaned over the railing and shouted: "Palace step guards!"

units.zh: 郎曰：「諾。」
units.en: The guards answered as one: "Aye!"
units.literal: The guards answered: "Yes!"

units.zh: 優旃曰：「汝雖長，何益，幸雨立。
units.en: You Zhan called out: "Tall as you are, what good does it do you? You get the privilege of standing in the rain.
units.literal: You Zhan said: "Though you are tall, what good does it do you? You are fortunate enough to stand in the rain.

units.zh: 我雖短也，幸休居。」
units.en: Short as I am, I get the privilege of sitting inside where it is dry."
units.literal: Though I am short, I am fortunate enough to sit and rest."

units.zh: 於是始皇使陛楯者得半相代。
units.en: At this, the First Emperor ordered that the guards be allowed to take turns, half on duty and half resting.
units.literal: Thereupon the First Emperor allowed the guards to take turns in shifts, with half relieved at a time.

units.zh: 始皇嘗議欲大苑囿，東至函谷關，西至雍、陳倉。
units.en: The First Emperor once proposed to vastly expand the imperial hunting park, stretching it east to Hangu Pass and west to Yong and Chencang.
units.literal: The First Emperor once proposed to greatly expand the imperial park, extending east to Hangu Pass and west to Yong and Chencang.

units.zh: 優旃曰：「善。
units.en: You Zhan said: "A splendid idea!
units.literal: You Zhan said: "Excellent.

units.zh: 多縱禽獸於其中，寇從東方來，令麋鹿觸之足矣。」
units.en: Fill it with game animals aplenty, and when the invaders come from the east, simply order the elk to charge them — that should be quite sufficient."
units.literal: Stock it with plenty of wild animals, and when invaders come from the east, just have the elk charge at them — that will be enough."

units.zh: 始皇以故輟止。
units.en: Because of this, the First Emperor abandoned the plan.
units.literal: The First Emperor therefore abandoned the plan.

units.zh: 二世立，又欲漆其城。
units.en: When the Second Emperor ascended the throne, he conceived the notion of lacquering the city walls.
units.literal: When the Second Emperor came to the throne, he wanted to lacquer the city walls.

units.zh: 優旃曰：「善。
units.en: You Zhan said: "A wonderful idea!
units.literal: You Zhan said: "Excellent.

units.zh: 主上雖無言，臣固將請之。
units.en: Even had Your Majesty not proposed it, your servant was just about to suggest it himself.
units.literal: Even if Your Majesty had not spoken, your servant was already going to propose it.

units.zh: 漆城雖於百姓愁費，然佳哉！
units.en: True, lacquering the walls will burden the people with grief and expense — but what a magnificent sight it will be!
units.literal: Although lacquering the walls would cause the people grief and expense, how magnificent it would be!

units.zh: 漆城蕩蕩，寇來不能上。
units.en: The lacquered walls will gleam so smooth and slippery that when invaders come, they will never be able to scale them.
units.literal: The lacquered walls will be smooth and gleaming — when invaders come, they will not be able to climb up.

units.zh: 即欲就之，易為漆耳，顧難為蔭室。」
units.en: The only difficulty is this: applying the lacquer is easy enough, but where on earth would we build a drying shed large enough to cover the walls while they cure?"
units.literal: If one wishes to carry this out, the lacquering itself is easy, but the hard part would be building a drying shed big enough to cover the walls."

units.zh: 於是二世笑之，以其故止。
units.en: The Second Emperor burst out laughing and dropped the idea.
units.literal: The Second Emperor laughed at this and abandoned the plan for this reason.

units.zh: 居無何，二世殺死，優旃歸漢，數年而卒。
units.en: Not long after, the Second Emperor was killed. You Zhan went over to the Han dynasty, and some years later he passed away.
units.literal: Not long after, the Second Emperor was killed. You Zhan submitted to Han, and after several years he died.

units.zh: 太史公曰：淳于髡仰天大笑，齊威王橫行。
units.en: The Grand Historian remarks: Chunyu Kun threw back his head and laughed to the heavens, and King Wei of Qi marched unchallenged across the land.
units.literal: The Grand Historian says: Chunyu Kun threw back his head and laughed at the sky, and King Wei of Qi swept all before him.

units.zh: 優孟搖頭而歌，負薪者以封。
units.en: You Meng shook his head and broke into song, and the man who carried firewood received a fief.
units.literal: You Meng shook his head and sang, and the firewood carrier was enfeoffed.

units.zh: 優旃臨檻疾呼，陛楯得以半更。
units.en: You Zhan leaned over the balustrade and cried out, and the guards were granted the mercy of half-shifts.
units.literal: You Zhan leaned over the railing and cried out, and the palace guards were allowed to take half-shifts.

units.zh: 豈不亦偉哉！
units.en: Were these men not also magnificent in their way!
units.literal: Is this not also magnificent!

units.zh: 褚先生曰：臣幸得以經術為郎，而好讀外家傳語。
units.en: Master Chu says: Your servant was fortunate enough to gain his position as a court gentleman through scholarship in the Classics, and he has always delighted in reading the traditions and tales of other schools.
units.literal: Master Chu says: Your servant was fortunate to be appointed a palace gentleman through his study of the Classics, and he has loved reading the traditions and stories of the various schools.

units.zh: 竊不遜讓，復作故事滑稽之語六章，編之於左。
units.en: With more boldness than modesty, I have composed six additional tales of wit and humor, which are appended below.
units.literal: Presumptuously and without modesty, I have composed six additional chapters of anecdotes and jests, appended below.

units.zh: 可以覽觀揚意，以示後世好事者讀之，以游心駭耳，以附益上方太史公之三章。
units.en: These may be perused for amusement and edification, and offered to curious readers of later ages for the pleasure of the mind and the surprise of the ear — appended here as a supplement to the Grand Historian's three tales above.
units.literal: These may be browsed and contemplated to elevate the mind, shown to curious readers of later generations for the delight of the imagination and the startling of the ears, appended as a supplement to the three chapters of the Grand Historian above.

units.zh: 武帝時有所幸倡郭舍人者，發言陳辭雖不合大道，然令人主和說。
units.en: In the time of Emperor Wu, there was a favored jester by the name of Guo Sheren. His words and quips may not have accorded with the great Way, but they never failed to put the emperor in good humor.
units.literal: During the time of Emperor Wu, there was a favored entertainer named Guo Sheren, whose speech and arguments, though they did not accord with the great Way, nevertheless pleased and amused the sovereign.

units.zh: 武帝少時，東武侯母常養帝，帝壯時，號之曰「大乳母」。
units.en: When Emperor Wu was a boy, the mother of the Marquis of Dongwu had served as his wet nurse. When he grew to manhood, he honored her with the title 'the Great Nurse.'
units.literal: When Emperor Wu was young, the mother of the Marquis of Dongwu had often nursed him. When the emperor grew up, he called her the 'Great Wet Nurse.'

units.zh: 率一月再朝。
units.en: She was received at court twice a month as a matter of course.
units.literal: On average, she had audience at court twice a month.

units.zh: 朝奏入，有詔使幸臣馬游卿以帛五十匹賜乳母，又奉飲糒飱養乳母。
units.en: Whenever she submitted a memorial, the emperor would order his favored minister Ma Youqing to bestow fifty bolts of silk upon the nurse, along with food and provisions for her maintenance.
units.literal: When her memorials were presented at court, there were edicts ordering the favored minister Ma Youqing to bestow fifty bolts of silk upon the wet nurse, and also to provide her with food and drink and provisions to support her.

units.zh: 乳母上書曰：「某所有公田，願得假倩之。」
units.en: The nurse petitioned the throne: "There are public fields at a certain place. I beg to be allowed to lease them."
units.literal: The wet nurse submitted a petition saying: "There are public fields at such-and-such a place; I wish to be allowed to lease them."

units.zh: 帝曰：「乳母欲得之乎？」
units.en: The emperor said: "The nurse wants them?"
units.literal: The emperor said: "The nurse wishes to have them?"

units.zh: 以賜乳母。
units.en: And he granted them to her.
units.literal: He bestowed them upon the nurse.

units.zh: 乳母所言，未嘗不聽。
units.en: Whatever the nurse requested, the emperor never refused.
units.literal: Whatever the nurse asked for, the emperor never failed to comply.

units.zh: 有詔得令乳母乘車行馳道中。
units.en: A special edict was issued granting the nurse the privilege of traveling by carriage on the imperial thoroughfare.
units.literal: An edict was issued permitting the nurse to ride in a carriage on the imperial roads.

units.zh: 當此之時，公卿大臣皆敬重乳母。
units.en: At this time, every minister and high official in the court treated the nurse with the greatest respect.
units.literal: At this time, the dukes, ministers, and great officials all treated the nurse with respect and deference.

units.zh: 乳母家子孫奴從者橫暴長安中，當道掣頓人車馬，奪人衣服。
units.en: The nurse's children, grandchildren, slaves, and attendants ran rampant through Chang'an. They blocked the roads, dragged people from their carts, and stripped the clothes from their backs.
units.literal: The children, grandchildren, slaves, and servants of the nurse's household acted with violent arrogance throughout Chang'an, seizing people's carriages and horses in the middle of the road and snatching their clothes.

units.zh: 聞於中，不忍致之法。
units.en: When word of this reached the emperor, he could not bring himself to punish her.
units.literal: When the emperor heard of this at court, he could not bear to subject her to the law.

units.zh: 有司請徙乳母家室，處之於邊。
units.en: The responsible officials petitioned to have the nurse's entire household banished to the frontier.
units.literal: The responsible officials petitioned to have the nurse's entire household relocated to the frontier.

units.zh: 奏可。
units.en: The petition was approved.
units.literal: The memorial was approved.

units.zh: 乳母當入至前，面見辭。
units.en: The nurse was to present herself before the emperor for a final audience to take her leave.
units.literal: The nurse was to enter the palace and come before the emperor to bid farewell in person.

units.zh: 乳母先見郭舍人，為下泣。
units.en: Before the audience, the nurse went to see Guo Sheren and wept before him.
units.literal: The nurse first went to see Guo Sheren, weeping before him.

units.zh: 舍人曰：「即入見辭去，疾步數還顧。」
units.en: Sheren told her: "When you go in to bid farewell, walk away briskly — but keep glancing back over your shoulder."
units.literal: Sheren said: "When you go in to take your leave, walk away quickly but keep turning back to look."

units.zh: 乳母如其言，謝去，疾步數還顧。
units.en: The nurse followed his instructions. She said her farewell and turned to leave, walking briskly but glancing back again and again.
units.literal: The nurse did as he said: she bid farewell and departed, walking quickly and turning back to look several times.

units.zh: 郭舍人疾言罵之曰：「咄！
units.en: Guo Sheren barked after her: "Bah!
units.literal: Guo Sheren shouted at her in a scolding tone: "Bah!

units.zh: 老女子！
units.en: You foolish old woman!
units.literal: Old woman!

units.zh: 何不疾行！
units.en: Get moving, won't you!
units.literal: Why don't you hurry along!

units.zh: 陛下已壯矣，寧尚須汝乳而活邪？
units.en: His Majesty is a grown man now — does he still need your breast to survive?
units.literal: His Majesty is a grown man now — does he still need your milk to live?

units.zh: 尚何還顧！」
units.en: What is there to keep looking back for!"
units.literal: What are you still looking back for!"

units.zh: 於是人主憐焉悲之，乃下詔止無徙乳母，罰謫譖之者。
units.en: At this, the emperor was overcome with pity and grief. He issued an edict revoking the nurse's banishment and punished those who had spoken against her.
units.literal: At this, the emperor was moved to pity and sorrow for her, and issued an edict rescinding the banishment of the nurse and punishing those who had slandered her.

units.zh: 武帝時，齊人有東方生名朔，以好古傳書，愛經術，多所博觀外家之語。
units.en: In the time of Emperor Wu, there was a man from Qi surnamed Dongfang, whose given name was Shuo. He was devoted to the ancient traditions, loved the study of the Classics, and had read widely in the writings of other schools.
units.literal: During the time of Emperor Wu, there was a man from Qi surnamed Dongfang and named Shuo, who loved the ancient traditions and writings, cherished the study of the Classics, and read widely in the works of the various schools.

units.zh: 朔初入長安，至公車上書，凡用三千奏牘。
units.en: When Shuo first arrived in Chang'an, he submitted a memorial through the Office of the Public Carriage. It filled three thousand bamboo tablets.
units.literal: When Shuo first came to Chang'an, he submitted a memorial at the Office of the Public Carriage, using a total of three thousand bamboo writing tablets.

units.zh: 公車令兩人共持舉其書，僅然能勝之。
units.en: The Director of the Public Carriage had two men lift the memorial together, and even then they could barely carry it.
units.literal: The Director of the Public Carriage needed two men working together to hold and lift his document, and they could barely manage it.

units.zh: 人主從上方讀之，止，輒乙其處，讀之二月乃盡。
units.en: The emperor read it through from beginning to end, marking his place with a notch each time he paused. It took him two full months to finish.
units.literal: The emperor read it from beginning to end; whenever he stopped, he would mark his place with a notch, and it took him two months to finish.

units.zh: 詔拜以為郎，常在側侍中。
units.en: By imperial edict, Shuo was appointed a palace gentleman and was always kept in attendance at the emperor's side.
units.literal: An edict was issued appointing him as a palace gentleman, and he was always at the emperor's side in attendance.

units.zh: 數召至前談語，人主未嘗不說也。
units.en: He was frequently called before the emperor for conversation, and the emperor never failed to be delighted.
units.literal: He was frequently summoned before the emperor to talk and converse, and the emperor was never anything but pleased.

units.zh: 時詔賜之食於前。
units.en: From time to time, the emperor ordered food to be served to him right there at court.
units.literal: From time to time the emperor would order food to be served to him in the imperial presence.

units.zh: 飯已，盡懷其餘肉持去，衣盡汙。
units.en: When the meal was done, he would stuff every last scrap of leftover meat into the folds of his robe and carry it off, leaving his clothes thoroughly stained with grease.
units.literal: After eating, he would stuff all the remaining meat into his clothes and carry it away, staining his garments completely.

units.zh: 數賜縑帛，檐揭而去。
units.en: Whenever the emperor bestowed bolts of silk upon him, he would sling them over his shoulder and stride away.
units.literal: He was frequently given gifts of silk, which he would carry off draped over his shoulders.

units.zh: 徒用所賜錢帛，取少婦於長安中好女。
units.en: He used every coin and bolt of silk he received to take young wives from among the most beautiful women of Chang'an.
units.literal: He spent all the money and silk he was given on taking young wives from among the beautiful women of Chang'an.

units.zh: 率取婦一歲所者即棄去，更取婦。
units.en: He would keep each wife for about a year before casting her aside and marrying a new one.
units.literal: As a rule, he would keep a wife for about a year and then abandon her, taking a new wife.

units.zh: 所賜錢財盡索之於女子。
units.en: Every bit of wealth the emperor bestowed on him was lavished upon women.
units.literal: All the money and wealth he was given was spent entirely on women.

units.zh: 人主左右諸郎半呼之「狂人」。
units.en: Half the gentlemen at court took to calling him 'the Madman.'
units.literal: Half of the palace gentlemen around the emperor called him 'the madman.'

units.zh: 人主聞之，曰：「令朔在事無為是行者，若等安能及之哉！」
units.en: When the emperor heard this, he said: "If Shuo held his office without indulging in such antics, how could the likes of you ever hope to match him!"
units.literal: When the emperor heard this, he said: "If Shuo conducted his affairs without engaging in such behavior, how could the likes of you ever match him!"

units.zh: 朔任其子為郎，又為侍謁者，常持節出使。
units.en: Shuo had his son appointed a palace gentleman. He himself also served as an attendant and reception officer, and was frequently sent on missions bearing the imperial tally.
units.literal: Shuo had his son appointed as a palace gentleman, and he himself also served as an attendant and reception officer, frequently carrying the imperial tally on diplomatic missions.

units.zh: 朔行殿中，郎謂之曰：「人皆以先生為狂。」
units.en: As Shuo was passing through the palace hall one day, a gentleman said to him: "Everyone thinks you are mad, sir."
units.literal: As Shuo was walking through the palace hall, a gentleman said to him: "Everyone considers the master to be mad."

units.zh: 朔曰：「如朔等，所謂避世於朝廷閒者也。
units.en: Shuo replied: "Men like me are what you might call recluses who hide from the world right here at court.
units.literal: Shuo said: "Men like me are what is called those who withdraw from the world within the court itself.

units.zh: 古之人，乃避世於深山中。」
units.en: The recluses of old fled into the deep mountains."
units.literal: The men of old withdrew from the world into the deep mountains."

units.zh: 時坐席中，酒酣，據地歌曰：「陸沈於俗，避世金馬門。
units.en: Once, deep into his cups at a banquet, he slapped the ground and sang: "Sunk in obscurity among the vulgar crowd, I hide from the world at the Gate of the Golden Horse.
units.literal: Once, sitting among the guests when the wine was flowing freely, he slapped the ground and sang: "Sinking into obscurity among the common world, I withdraw from the world at the Gate of the Golden Horse.

units.zh: 宮殿中可以避世全身，何必深山之中，蒿廬之下。」
units.en: Within these palace walls a man can hide from the world and keep himself whole — what need is there for deep mountains and thatched huts?"
units.literal: Within the palace one can withdraw from the world and preserve one's life — why must one go to the deep mountains and dwell in a thatched hut?"

units.zh: 金馬門者，宦［者］署門也，門傍有銅馬，故謂之曰「金馬門」。
units.en: The Gate of the Golden Horse was the entrance to the offices of the palace attendants. A bronze horse stood beside the gate, which is why it was called the "Gate of the Golden Horse."
units.literal: The Gate of the Golden Horse was the gate of the office of the palace attendants. Beside the gate there was a bronze horse, which is why it was called the 'Gate of the Golden Horse.'

units.zh: 時會聚宮下博士諸先生與論議，共難之曰：「蘇秦、張儀一當萬乘之主，而都卿相之位，澤及後世。
units.en: Once, the court academicians and scholars assembled and challenged him in debate: "Su Qin and Zhang Yi each won audience with the mightiest rulers of their age, rose to the rank of minister and chancellor, and their influence was felt for generations to come.
units.literal: Once, the court scholars and academicians gathered and debated with him, challenging him together: "Su Qin and Zhang Yi each faced the rulers of ten-thousand-chariot states, rose to the positions of minister and chancellor, and their benefits reached to later generations.

units.zh: 今子大夫修先王之術，慕聖人之義，諷誦詩書百家之言，不可勝數。
units.en: Now you, sir, have cultivated the arts of the former kings, revered the righteous ways of the sages, and committed to memory the Odes, the Documents, and the writings of the hundred schools — more than can be counted.
units.literal: Now you, sir, have studied the arts of the former kings, admired the righteous ways of the sages, and recited the Odes, the Documents, and the words of the hundred schools — too numerous to count.

units.zh: 著於竹帛，自以為海內無雙，即可謂博聞辯智矣。
units.en: Your writings fill scroll after scroll, and you consider yourself without peer in all the realm — a man of vast learning and eloquent wit, by any measure.
units.literal: Your writings fill bamboo and silk, and you consider yourself without equal in the realm — one might indeed call you broadly learned and eloquently wise.

units.zh: 然悉力盡忠以事聖帝，曠日持久，積數十年，官不過侍郎，位不過執戟，意者尚有遺行邪？
units.en: And yet, for all your exhausting loyalty in the emperor's service, over the course of decades your office has never risen above Attendant Gentleman and your rank has never surpassed Halberd-Bearer. Could it be that there is something wanting in your conduct?
units.literal: Yet despite exhausting your strength and devotion in serving the sage emperor, over the long course of decades, your office has never risen above Attendant Gentleman, your rank never beyond Halberd-Bearer. Could there perhaps still be some fault in your conduct?

units.zh: 其故何也？」
units.en: Why might that be?"
units.literal: What is the reason for this?"

units.zh: 東方生曰：「是固非子所能備也。
units.en: Dongfang Shuo replied: "This is something that lies entirely beyond your understanding.
units.literal: Master Dongfang said: "This is something you are simply unable to comprehend.

units.zh: 彼一時也，此一時也，豈可同哉！
units.en: Those were different times, and these are different times — how can the two be compared!
units.literal: That was one era, and this is another — how can they be compared!

units.zh: 夫張儀、蘇秦之時，周室大壞，諸侯不朝，力政爭權，相禽以兵，并為十二國，未有雌雄，得士者彊，失士者亡，故說聽行通，身處尊位，澤及後世，子孫長榮。
units.en: In the days of Zhang Yi and Su Qin, the house of Zhou lay in ruins. The feudal lords no longer came to court; they governed by force and vied for supremacy, waging war upon one another. The world was divided among a dozen states, with no clear victor. Those who won talented men grew strong; those who lost them perished. And so these men's counsel was heeded, their plans put into action. They rose to the highest offices, their influence endured for generations, and their descendants prospered long after them.
units.literal: In the time of Zhang Yi and Su Qin, the house of Zhou was in great ruin, the feudal lords no longer attended court, they governed by force and contended for power, seizing one another through warfare, merged into twelve states with no clear victor — those who won scholars grew strong, those who lost them perished. Therefore, their counsel was heeded, their proposals accepted, they occupied the highest positions, their influence reached later generations, and their descendants prospered for ages.

units.zh: 今非然也。
units.en: Today, things are entirely different.
units.literal: Now it is not so.

units.zh: 聖帝在上，德流天下，諸侯賓服，威振四夷，連四海之外以為席，安於覆盂，天下平均，合為一家，動發舉事，猶如運之掌中。
units.en: A sage emperor reigns above, and his virtue flows to every corner of the realm. The feudal lords submit in deference, his authority makes the barbarians of the four directions tremble. The lands beyond the four seas lie before him like a spread mat, as steady as an overturned bowl. All under heaven is unified and at peace, joined as one great family, and every enterprise the emperor undertakes is as effortless as turning an object in the palm of his hand.
units.literal: A sage emperor sits on the throne, his virtue flows throughout the realm, the feudal lords submit as guests, his authority shakes the four barbarian peoples, the lands beyond the four seas are spread like a mat, as stable as an overturned bowl, the empire is level and equal, united as one family, and every undertaking he sets in motion is as easy as turning something in the palm of his hand.

units.zh: 賢與不肖，何以異哉？
units.en: In such an age, what difference is there between the worthy and the unworthy?
units.literal: Between the worthy and the unworthy, what difference is there?

units.zh: 方今以天下之大，士民之眾，竭精馳說，并進輻湊者，不可勝數。
units.en: Now, given the vastness of the empire and the sheer multitude of its people, those who pour out their talents and hawk their ideas, pressing forward from every direction — they are beyond counting.
units.literal: At present, given the vastness of the empire and the multitude of scholars and common people, those who exhaust their talents and rush about peddling their ideas, pressing forward and converging from all sides, cannot be counted.

units.zh: 悉力慕義，困於衣食，或失門戶。
units.en: They devote every ounce of their strength to the pursuit of virtue, yet they can scarcely clothe and feed themselves, and some have lost even their family standing.
units.literal: They devote all their strength to pursuing righteousness, yet are reduced to poverty in food and clothing, and some even lose their family standing.

units.zh: 使張儀、蘇秦與仆并生於今之世，曾不能得掌故，安敢望常侍侍郎乎！
units.en: If Zhang Yi and Su Qin were alive today, born into this same age as I, they could not so much as land a post as a petty archivist — how then would they dare dream of becoming Regular Attendant or Attendant Gentleman!
units.literal: If Zhang Yi and Su Qin were born together with me in this present age, they could not even obtain the post of a minor archivist — how would they dare hope for the rank of Regular Attendant or Attendant Gentleman!

units.zh: 傳曰：『天下無害菑，雖有聖人，無所施其才；
units.en: As the tradition has it: 'When the world is free of calamity and ruin, even a sage has no occasion to display his talents.
units.literal: The tradition says: 'When the world is free from harm and disaster, though there be sages, they have no occasion to exercise their talents;

units.zh: 上下和同，雖有賢者，無所立功。』
units.en: When those above and below are in harmony, even a worthy man has no occasion to win distinction.'
units.literal: When high and low are harmonious and united, though there be worthy men, they have no occasion to establish merit.'

units.zh: 故曰時異則事異。
units.en: The saying goes: different times call for different measures.
units.literal: Therefore, it is said: when the times change, affairs change with them.

units.zh: 雖然，安可以不務修身乎？
units.en: And yet, how can a man neglect the cultivation of his own character?
units.literal: Even so, how can one fail to devote oneself to self-cultivation?

units.zh: 《詩》曰：『鼓鐘于宮，聲聞于外。
units.en: As the Odes say: 'When drums and bells sound within the palace, their music carries beyond the walls.
units.literal: The Odes say: 'When drums and bells sound in the palace, their sound is heard outside.

units.zh: 鶴鳴九皋，聲聞于天。』。
units.en: The crane cries from the deepest marsh, and its voice reaches the heavens.'
units.literal: The crane cries at the ninth marsh, and its voice is heard in heaven.'

units.zh: 茍能修身，何患不榮！
units.en: If a man can truly cultivate himself, what need has he to worry that recognition will not come!
units.literal: If one can cultivate oneself, why worry about not being honored!

units.zh: 太公躬行仁義七十二年，逢文王，得行其說，封於齊，七百歲而不絕。
units.en: The Grand Duke practiced benevolence and righteousness in person for seventy-two years before he met King Wen, gained the chance to put his ideas into practice, and was enfeoffed in Qi — where his line endured unbroken for seven hundred years.
units.literal: The Grand Duke personally practiced benevolence and righteousness for seventy-two years before he met King Wen, was able to put his ideas into action, and was enfeoffed in Qi, where his line endured for seven hundred years without interruption.

units.zh: 此士之所以日夜孜孜，修學行道，不敢止也。
units.en: This is why the scholar toils day and night without respite, cultivating his learning and walking the Way, never daring to cease.
units.literal: This is why scholars toil day and night without rest, studying and walking the Way, never daring to stop.

units.zh: 今世之處士，時雖不用，崛然獨立，塊然獨處，上觀許由，下察接輿，策同范蠡，忠合子胥，天下和平，與義相扶，寡偶少徒，固其常也。
units.en: The recluse scholars of our age, though the times have no use for them, stand tall and solitary, dwelling apart in their grandeur. They look upward to Xu You for inspiration and downward to Jie Yu; their stratagems rival those of Fan Li, and their loyalty matches that of Wu Zixu. The world is at peace, and they sustain themselves through righteousness. That they have few companions and fewer followers — this is simply their lot.
units.literal: The recluse scholars of our age, though the times do not employ them, stand towering and alone, dwelling in solitary grandeur. They look up to Xu You, study Jie Yu below, their strategy matches Fan Li, their loyalty accords with Zixu. The world is at peace, and they support each other with righteousness. Having few companions and fewer followers — this is simply their normal lot.

units.zh: 子何疑於余哉！」
units.en: Why then do you question me!"
units.literal: Why should you doubt me!"

units.zh: 於是諸先生默然無以應也。
units.en: At this, every one of the scholars fell silent, with not a word to say in reply.
units.literal: At this, all the scholars fell silent, having nothing to say in reply.

units.zh: 建章宮後閤重櫟中有物出焉，其狀似麋。
units.en: In the rear gallery of the Jianzhang Palace, amid a dense stand of oaks, a strange creature appeared. Its form resembled that of an elk.
units.literal: In the rear courtyard of the Jianzhang Palace, among a thicket of oaks, a creature appeared whose shape resembled an elk.

units.zh: 以聞，武帝往臨視之。
units.en: When word reached the throne, Emperor Wu went in person to inspect it.
units.literal: When the report was made, Emperor Wu went in person to look at it.

units.zh: 問左右群臣習事通經術者，莫能知。
units.en: He questioned the attending ministers — those versed in affairs and learned in the Classics — but none of them could identify it.
units.literal: He asked those around him, the ministers who were versed in affairs and learned in the Classics, but none could identify it.

units.zh: 詔東方朔視之。
units.en: He ordered Dongfang Shuo to come and take a look.
units.literal: An edict was issued for Dongfang Shuo to come examine it.

units.zh: 朔曰：「臣知之，願賜美酒粱飯大飱臣，臣乃言。」
units.en: Shuo said: "Your servant knows what it is. But first, I beg that Your Majesty reward me with fine wine and a feast of the best millet — and only then will I speak."
units.literal: Shuo said: "Your servant knows what it is. I beg that you bestow fine wine and millet rice upon your servant as a great feast, and then I will speak."

units.zh: 詔曰：「可。」
units.en: The emperor said: "Granted."
units.literal: The edict said: "Granted."

units.zh: 已又曰：「某所有公田魚池蒲葦數頃，陛下以賜臣，臣朔乃言。」
units.en: After the feast, Shuo added: "At a certain place there are public fields with fishponds and beds of rushes and reeds — several qing in area. If Your Majesty bestows them upon me, then I shall tell you what the creature is."
units.literal: After this he further said: "There are public fields with fish ponds and beds of rushes and reeds at such-and-such a place, several qing in area. I beg Your Majesty to bestow them upon your servant, and then I, Shuo, will speak."

units.zh: 詔曰：「可。」
units.en: The emperor replied: "Granted."
units.literal: The edict said: "Granted."

units.zh: 於是朔乃肯言，曰：「所謂騶牙者也。
units.en: Only then did Shuo consent to speak. He said: "This is what is known as a zouya.
units.literal: Only then did Shuo consent to speak, saying: "It is what is called a zouya.

units.zh: 遠方當來歸義，而騶牙先見。
units.en: When people from distant lands are about to come and submit in allegiance, the zouya appears as a harbinger.
units.literal: When distant peoples are about to come and submit to righteousness, the zouya appears beforehand.

units.zh: 其齒前后若一，齊等無牙，故謂之騶牙。」
units.en: Its teeth are uniform from front to back, even and without tusks — which is why it is called the zouya, the creature of orderly teeth."
units.literal: Its teeth, front and back, are all alike, even and without tusks — therefore it is called the 'zouya' (orderly teeth)."

units.zh: 其後一歲所，匈奴混邪王果將十萬眾來降漢。
units.en: About a year later, just as Shuo had predicted, the Xiongnu King Hunye led a hundred thousand of his people to surrender to the Han.
units.literal: About a year later, the Xiongnu King Hunye did indeed lead a force of a hundred thousand to surrender to Han.

units.zh: 乃復賜東方生錢財甚多。
units.en: The emperor once again lavished Dongfang Shuo with generous gifts of money and treasure.
units.literal: The emperor once again bestowed upon Dongfang Shuo a great deal of money and gifts.

units.zh: 至老，朔且死時，諫曰：「《詩》云『營營青蠅，止于蕃。
units.en: In old age, when Shuo lay on his deathbed, he offered a final admonition: "The Odes say, 'The buzzing green flies settle on the fence.
units.literal: In his old age, when Shuo was about to die, he admonished the emperor, saying: "The Odes say, 'The buzzing green flies settle on the fence.

units.zh: 愷悌君子，無信讒言。
units.en: O kind and gracious lord, give no credit to slanderous words.
units.literal: O gentle and kind lord, do not believe slanderous words.

units.zh: 讒言罔極，交亂四國』。
units.en: Slander knows no bounds, and throws the four quarters of the realm into confusion.'
units.literal: Slanderous words know no limit, and bring turmoil to the four quarters.'

units.zh: 願陛下遠巧佞，退讒言。」
units.en: I beg Your Majesty to keep your distance from the cunning and the sycophantic, and to cast aside all slanderous counsel."
units.literal: I beg Your Majesty to keep far from the cunning and the sycophantic, and to reject slanderous speech."

units.zh: 帝曰：「今顧東方朔多善言？」
units.en: The emperor said: "Since when has Dongfang Shuo had so many wise things to say?"
units.literal: The emperor said: "How is it that Dongfang Shuo now speaks so many good words?"

units.zh: 怪之。
units.en: He thought it most peculiar.
units.literal: He found it strange.

units.zh: 居無幾何，朔果病死。
units.en: Not long after, Shuo fell ill and died, just as one might have expected.
units.literal: Not long afterward, Shuo indeed fell ill and died.

units.zh: 傳曰：「鳥之將死，其鳴也哀；
units.en: As the saying goes: "When a bird is about to die, its song turns mournful.
units.literal: The tradition says: "When a bird is about to die, its song is mournful;

units.zh: 人之將死，其言也善。」
units.en: When a man is about to die, his words turn to wisdom."
units.literal: When a man is about to die, his words are good."

units.zh: 此之謂也。
units.en: This is precisely what the saying means.
units.literal: This is what the saying refers to.

units.zh: 武帝時，大將軍衛青者，衛后兄也，封為長平侯。
units.en: In the time of Emperor Wu, the Grand General Wei Qing — brother of Empress Wei — held the title of Marquis of Changping.
units.literal: During the time of Emperor Wu, the Grand General Wei Qing was the brother of Empress Wei and had been enfeoffed as the Marquis of Changping.

units.zh: 從軍擊匈奴，至余吾水上而還，斬首捕虜，有功來歸，詔賜金千斤。
units.en: He had led an expedition against the Xiongnu, pushing as far as the Yuwu River before turning back, taking heads and capturing prisoners. He returned victorious, and the emperor rewarded him with a thousand catties of gold.
units.literal: He had led the army to attack the Xiongnu, advancing as far as the Yu Wu River before returning, cutting off heads and capturing prisoners. Having won merit and returned, the emperor awarded him a thousand catties of gold.

units.zh: 將軍出宮門，齊人東郭先生以方士待詔公車，當道遮衛將軍車，拜謁曰：「願白事。」
units.en: As the general was leaving the palace, a man from Qi named Dongguo Xiansheng — who had been waiting as a fangshi at the Office of the Public Carriage — stepped into the road and blocked the general's carriage. He bowed and said: "I wish to offer a word of counsel."
units.literal: As the general was leaving the palace gate, a man from Qi named Dongguo Xiansheng, who had been waiting as a fangshi at the Office of the Public Carriage, blocked the general's carriage in the road, bowed and said: "I wish to present a matter to you."

units.zh: 將軍止車前，東郭先生旁車言曰：「王夫人新得幸於上，家貧。
units.en: The general stopped his carriage, and Dongguo Xiansheng spoke from beside it: "Lady Wang has recently won the emperor's favor, but her family is poor.
units.literal: The general halted his carriage, and Dongguo Xiansheng spoke from beside the carriage: "Lady Wang has recently won the emperor's favor, but her family is poor.

units.zh: 今將軍得金千斤，誠以其半賜王夫人之親，人主聞之必喜。
units.en: Now the general has received a thousand catties of gold. If you were to present half of it to Lady Wang's family as a gift, the emperor will surely be delighted when he hears of it.
units.literal: Now the general has received a thousand catties of gold. If you would sincerely give half to Lady Wang's family, the emperor will surely be pleased when he hears of it.

units.zh: 此所謂奇策便計也。」
units.en: This is what you might call a masterstroke of expedient counsel."
units.literal: This is what is called an ingenious strategy and a convenient plan."

units.zh: 衛將軍謝之曰：「先生幸告之以便計，請奉教。」
units.en: General Wei thanked him: "The master has been kind enough to share this excellent counsel. I shall follow your advice."
units.literal: General Wei thanked him, saying: "The master has been so kind as to tell me this advantageous plan. I will respectfully follow your instructions."

units.zh: 於是衛將軍乃以五百金為王夫人之親壽。
units.en: And so General Wei presented five hundred catties of gold to the family of Lady Wang as a gift.
units.literal: Thereupon General Wei presented five hundred catties of gold to Lady Wang's family as a gift of congratulation.

units.zh: 王夫人以聞武帝。
units.en: Lady Wang brought word of this to Emperor Wu.
units.literal: Lady Wang reported this to Emperor Wu.

units.zh: 帝曰：「大將軍不知為此。」
units.en: The emperor said: "The Grand General would never have thought of this on his own."
units.literal: The emperor said: "The Grand General would not have known to do this on his own."

units.zh: 問之安所受計策，對曰：「受之待詔者東郭先生。」
units.en: Asked who had given him the idea, the general answered: "It was a scholar-in-waiting by the name of Dongguo Xiansheng."
units.literal: When asked from whom he had received this plan, the general replied: "From a scholar-in-waiting named Dongguo Xiansheng."

units.zh: 詔召東郭先生，拜以為郡都尉。
units.en: The emperor summoned Dongguo Xiansheng and appointed him Commandant of a commandery.
units.literal: An edict summoned Dongguo Xiansheng, and he was appointed Commandant of a commandery.

units.zh: 東郭先生久待詔公車，貧困饑寒，衣敝，履不完。
units.en: Dongguo Xiansheng had languished for years at the Office of the Public Carriage, impoverished and half-starved, his clothes in tatters and his shoes falling apart.
units.literal: Dongguo Xiansheng had long waited at the Office of the Public Carriage, enduring poverty, hunger, and cold; his clothes were worn out and his shoes had no soles.

units.zh: 行雪中，履有上無下，足盡踐地。
units.en: When he walked through the snow, his shoes had uppers but no soles — his bare feet trod directly upon the frozen ground.
units.literal: When walking in the snow, his shoes had uppers but no soles, and his feet trod directly upon the ground.

units.zh: 道中人笑之，東郭先生應之曰：「誰能履行雪中，令人視之，其上履也，其履下處乃似人足者乎？」
units.en: Passersby laughed at him. Dongguo Xiansheng retorted: "Who else can walk through the snow and leave tracks that show shoes on top and bare human feet below?"
units.literal: People on the road laughed at him. Dongguo Xiansheng replied to them: "Who else can walk through the snow and leave prints that look like shoes on top and bare human feet on the bottom?"

units.zh: 及其拜為二千石，佩青緺出宮門，行謝主人。
units.en: When at last he was appointed to the rank of two-thousand-shi, he strode out the palace gate wearing a blue-green sash of office, and went to pay his respects to his former host.
units.literal: When he was appointed to the rank of two thousand shi, wearing a blue-green sash, he went out the palace gate to pay his respects to his former host.

units.zh: 故所以同官待詔者，等比祖道於都門外。
units.en: His former colleagues from the waiting list all gathered outside the capital gate to see him off with a farewell banquet.
units.literal: His former colleagues who had been waiting together with him at the Office all came to see him off with a farewell feast outside the capital gate.

units.zh: 榮華道路，立名當世。
units.en: He rode out in splendor, his reputation made in the eyes of all his contemporaries.
units.literal: He brought glory to the roads he traveled and established his name in his own time.

units.zh: 此所謂衣褐懷寶者也。
units.en: This is what the ancients meant by the man who wears coarse cloth but carries a jewel in his breast.
units.literal: This is what is called one who wears coarse cloth but carries treasure within.

units.zh: 當其貧困時，人莫省視；
units.en: When he was poor and destitute, not a soul spared him a glance.
units.literal: When he was poor and in difficulty, no one gave him a second glance;

units.zh: 至其貴也，乃爭附之。
units.en: But the moment he rose to honor, everyone scrambled to attach themselves to him.
units.literal: When he became honored, everyone scrambled to attach themselves to him.

units.zh: 諺曰：「相馬失之瘦，相士失之貧。」
units.en: As the proverb says: "In judging horses, leanness misleads you; in judging men, poverty misleads you."
units.literal: The proverb says: "In judging horses, one is misled by thinness; in judging scholars, one is misled by poverty."

units.zh: 其此之謂邪？
units.en: Is this not exactly what the proverb means?
units.literal: Is this not what the saying refers to?

units.zh: 王夫人病甚，人主至自往問之曰：「子當為王，欲安所置之？」
units.en: When Lady Wang fell gravely ill, the emperor visited her in person and asked: "Your son is to be made a king. Where would you like his kingdom to be?"
units.literal: Lady Wang fell gravely ill, and the emperor went in person to visit her, saying: "Your son shall be made a king. Where would you like him to be placed?"

units.zh: 對曰：「願居洛陽。」
units.en: She answered: "I wish him to be in Luoyang."
units.literal: She replied: "I would like him to reside in Luoyang."

units.zh: 人主曰：「不可。
units.en: The emperor said: "That is not possible.
units.literal: The emperor said: "That cannot be done.

units.zh: 洛陽有武庫、敖倉，當關口，天下咽喉。
units.en: Luoyang holds the Imperial Arsenal and the Ao Granary. It commands the passes and sits at the throat of the empire.
units.literal: Luoyang has the Imperial Arsenal and the Ao Granary, it guards the pass, and it is the throat of the empire.

units.zh: 自先帝以來，傳不為置王。
units.en: Since the time of our founding ancestors, the tradition has been never to establish a king there.
units.literal: Since the time of the former emperors, the tradition has been not to establish a king there.

units.zh: 然關東國莫大於齊，可以為齊王。」
units.en: However, of all the kingdoms east of the passes, none is greater than Qi. He shall be made King of Qi."
units.literal: However, among the kingdoms east of the pass, none is greater than Qi. He may be made King of Qi."

units.zh: 王夫人以手擊頭，呼「幸甚」。
units.en: Lady Wang pressed her hand to her forehead and exclaimed: "How blessed we are!"
units.literal: Lady Wang struck her forehead with her hand and cried out, "How fortunate!"

units.zh: 王夫人死，號曰「齊王太后薨」。
units.en: When Lady Wang died, the announcement read: "The Queen Dowager of Qi has passed away."
units.literal: When Lady Wang died, it was announced as "the death of the Queen Dowager of Qi."

units.zh: 昔者，齊王使淳于髡獻鵠於楚。
units.en: Once, in the old days, the King of Qi sent Chunyu Kun to present a swan as a gift to the King of Chu.
units.literal: In former times, the King of Qi sent Chunyu Kun to present a swan-goose to the King of Chu.

units.zh: 出邑門，道飛其鵠，徒揭空籠，造詐成辭，往見楚王曰：「齊王使臣來獻鵠，過於水上，不忍鵠之渴，出而飲之，去我飛亡。
units.en: Just outside the city gate, the swan took flight and escaped. Kun was left holding nothing but an empty cage. He fashioned a plausible story and went to see the King of Chu: "The King of Qi sent your servant to present a swan. As I was crossing a stream, I could not bear to see it suffer from thirst, so I took it out to let it drink — and it flew away.
units.literal: Upon leaving the city gate, the swan flew away on the road. Kun was left holding up the empty cage. He fabricated a deceitful excuse and went to see the King of Chu, saying: "The King of Qi sent your servant to present a swan. As I was passing over water, I could not bear the swan's thirst, so I let it out to drink, and it flew away from me.

units.zh: 吾欲刺腹絞頸而死。
units.en: I wanted to cut my belly open or hang myself.
units.literal: I wished to stab my belly or strangle myself and die.

units.zh: 恐人之議吾王以鳥獸之故令士自傷殺也。
units.en: But I feared that people would say my king had driven a man to his death over a mere bird.
units.literal: But I feared people would criticize my king for causing a gentleman to harm himself over a bird.

units.zh: 鵠，毛物，多相類者，吾欲買而代之，是不信而欺吾王也。
units.en: The swan is a feathered creature, and many of them look alike. I thought of buying another to take its place — but that would have been dishonest and a deception of my king.
units.literal: A swan is a feathered creature, and many look alike. I thought of buying a replacement, but that would be faithless and a deception of my king.

units.zh: 欲赴佗國奔亡，痛吾兩主使不通。
units.en: I thought of fleeing to another state, but it grieved me that the diplomatic exchange between our two sovereigns would be severed.
units.literal: I wished to flee to another state, but I grieved that this would cause the missions between our two rulers to be cut off.

units.zh: 故來服過，叩頭受罪大王。」
units.en: And so I have come to confess my transgression, prostrate myself, and accept whatever punishment Your Majesty sees fit to impose."
units.literal: Therefore, I have come to confess my fault, kowtow, and accept punishment from the Great King."

units.zh: 楚王曰：「善，齊王有信士若此哉！」
units.en: The King of Chu exclaimed: "Wonderful! So the King of Qi has men of such integrity!"
units.literal: The King of Chu said: "Excellent! So the King of Qi has faithful men like this!"

units.zh: 厚賜之，財倍鵠在也。
units.en: He showered Kun with generous gifts — worth twice what the swan itself would have been.
units.literal: He lavished generous gifts upon him, and the value was double what the swan would have been worth.

units.zh: 武帝時，徵北海太守詣行在所。
units.en: In the time of Emperor Wu, the Governor of Beihai was summoned to present himself before the emperor at his traveling court.
units.literal: During the time of Emperor Wu, the Governor of Beihai was summoned to present himself at the emperor's traveling headquarters.

units.zh: 有文學卒史王先生者，自請與太守俱，「吾有益於君」，君許之。
units.en: A scholarly clerk by the name of Wang Xiansheng asked to accompany him, declaring: "I will be of service to you, my lord." The governor agreed.
units.literal: There was a scholarly clerk named Wang Xiansheng who asked to accompany the governor, saying "I will be of benefit to you, my lord." The governor consented.

units.zh: 諸府掾功曹白云：「王先生嗜酒，多言少實，恐不可與俱。」
units.en: The governor's staff and merit officer warned him: "Wang Xiansheng is a drunkard — all talk and no substance. We fear it would be a mistake to bring him along."
units.literal: The various clerks and the merit officer of the governor's staff warned: "Wang Xiansheng is fond of wine and talks much but accomplishes little. We fear he should not be taken along."

units.zh: 太守曰：「先生意欲行，不可逆。」
units.en: The governor replied: "The master wishes to come. It would be wrong to refuse him."
units.literal: The governor said: "The master wishes to go. One cannot refuse him."

units.zh: 遂與俱。
units.en: And so they traveled together.
units.literal: So they went together.

units.zh: 行至宮下，待詔宮府門。
units.en: When they arrived at the palace, the governor waited for his summons at the gate of the palace offices.
units.literal: They traveled to the palace and waited for the imperial summons at the gate of the palace offices.

units.zh: 王先生徒懷錢沽酒，與衛卒仆射飲，日醉，不視其太守。
units.en: Wang Xiansheng, for his part, simply pulled coins from his robe to buy wine and spent his days drinking with the guards and their captain, getting drunk every day and paying the governor no attention whatsoever.
units.literal: Wang Xiansheng simply tucked money into his robe, bought wine, and drank with the guards and their captain, getting drunk every day, paying no attention to his governor.

units.zh: 太守入跪拜。
units.en: When the governor was finally called in, he knelt and bowed before the emperor.
units.literal: The governor went in to kneel and bow before the emperor.

units.zh: 王先生謂戶郎曰：「幸為我呼吾君至門內遙語。」
units.en: Wang Xiansheng said to the gate guard: "Would you be so kind as to call my lord just inside the gate? I wish to have a word with him from here."
units.literal: Wang Xiansheng said to the gate guard: "Please call my lord to come just inside the gate so I may speak with him from a distance."

units.zh: 戶郎為呼太守。
units.en: The guard summoned the governor.
units.literal: The gate guard called the governor.

units.zh: 太守來，望見王先生。
units.en: The governor came out and saw Wang Xiansheng waiting.
units.literal: The governor came and caught sight of Wang Xiansheng.

units.zh: 王先生曰：「天子即問君何以治北海令無盜賊，君對曰何哉？」
units.en: Wang Xiansheng asked: "When the Son of Heaven asks you how you governed Beihai so that there were no bandits, what do you plan to say?"
units.literal: Wang Xiansheng said: "When the Son of Heaven asks how you governed Beihai so that there were no bandits, what will you answer?"

units.zh: 對曰：「選擇賢材，各任之以其能，賞異等，罰不肖。」
units.en: The governor replied: "I would say that I selected worthy men of talent, appointed each according to his abilities, rewarded the outstanding, and punished the unfit."
units.literal: The governor replied: "I selected worthy and talented men, appointed each according to his ability, rewarded those who excelled, and punished the incompetent."

units.zh: 王先生曰：「對如是，是自譽自伐功，不可也。
units.en: Wang Xiansheng said: "If you answer like that, you will be praising yourself and boasting of your own merits — that will never do.
units.literal: Wang Xiansheng said: "To answer like that is to praise yourself and boast of your own merits — that will not do.

units.zh: 願君對言，非臣之力，盡陛下神靈威武所變化也。」
units.en: I suggest you answer like this: 'It was not through any effort of mine, but entirely through the divine spirit and martial power of Your Majesty that this transformation was wrought.'"
units.literal: I hope you will answer by saying: 'It was not through your servant's own efforts, but entirely through the divine spirit and martial might of Your Majesty that this transformation was achieved.'"

units.zh: 太守曰：「諾。」
units.en: The governor agreed: "Very well."
units.literal: The governor said: "Very well."

units.zh: 召入，至于殿下，有詔問之曰：「何於治北海，令盜賊不起？」
units.en: The governor was summoned before the throne. The emperor asked: "How is it that you governed Beihai so that not a single bandit arose?"
units.literal: He was summoned in and came before the hall. An imperial question was put to him: "How did you govern Beihai so that bandits did not arise?"

units.zh: 叩頭對言：「非臣之力，盡陛下神靈威武之所變化也。」
units.en: He prostrated himself and answered: "It was not through any effort of mine, but entirely through the divine spirit and martial power of Your Majesty that this transformation was wrought."
units.literal: He kowtowed and replied: "It was not through your servant's efforts, but entirely through the divine spirit and martial might of Your Majesty that this transformation was achieved."

units.zh: 武帝大笑，曰：「於呼！
units.en: Emperor Wu burst out laughing: "Ha!
units.literal: Emperor Wu laughed heartily and said: "Oh!

units.zh: 安得長者之語而稱之！
units.en: Where on earth did you pick up such a dignified turn of phrase!
units.literal: Where did you learn the words of an elder to speak them so!

units.zh: 安所受之？」
units.en: Who taught you to say that?"
units.literal: From whom did you receive this?"

units.zh: 對曰：「受之文學卒史。」
units.en: The governor answered: "It was my scholarly clerk who coached me."
units.literal: He replied: "I received it from a scholarly clerk."

units.zh: 帝曰：「今安在？」
units.en: The emperor asked: "Where is this man now?"
units.literal: The emperor said: "Where is he now?"

units.zh: 對曰：「在宮府門外。」
units.en: The governor replied: "He is outside the palace gate."
units.literal: He replied: "Outside the palace gate."

units.zh: 有詔召拜王先生為水衡丞，以北海太守為水衡都尉。
units.en: The emperor issued an edict appointing Wang Xiansheng as Assistant Superintendent of Waterways, and the Governor of Beihai was made Superintendent of Waterways.
units.literal: An edict was issued summoning and appointing Wang Xiansheng as the Assistant to the Superintendent of Waterways, and the Governor of Beihai was appointed Superintendent of Waterways.

units.zh: 傳曰：「美言可以市，尊行可以加人。
